input.summary:
Full source-fidelity preflight completed on p15. I read input/brief.md (formalities only: applicant/inventor Nimo Rotem, no priority claim, no federal support — matched against draft/02 and draft/03, both "Not applicable"), input/conversation.md (single USER passage, a truncated duplicate of the disclosure's first three paragraphs), and input/disclosure.md (the operative authority), then traced every claim limitation, every numbered part, every description paragraph, and all four figure briefs.

Claims: all 16 traced. Claim 1 elements (plurality of connector channels; contactor between branch and respective connector; connector current sensor measuring delivered connector current; control-pilot interface; local connector identifier; branch current sensor upstream of the contactors; controller coupled to pilot interfaces, sensors, contactors and branch sensor; stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy-deficit value; per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve; minimum-sustaining-first then deficit distribution; pilot send and connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command; verification-interval-gated one-at-a-time shedding in a stored order until below limit) each map to exact disclosure sentences. Claim 2 (re-measure after each opening, open no further once below) is the disclosure's "opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit". Claim 3 = the three reclosure conditions verbatim in substance. Claim 4 = welded-contactor/leakage-threshold, inhibit of the other contactors on the same branch, local fault indicator. Claim 5 = "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus". Claims 6–8 = network interface, signed local token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation subject to the last accepted limit and the independent branch-current safety process, token-gated new sessions with expiry, tamper-evident meter sequence uploaded on return. Claims 9–10 and 16 = the service-input mapping procedure and the store-only-on-agreement rule. Method claims 11–16 mirror the apparatus claims with no added matter. The claim-1/11 trigger "send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit" was checked specifically and traced to "staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond" together with "after a reduced pilot command"; it narrows rather than adds.

Numerals: all 25 ledger entries (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140, 202–216) appear once each with a single consistent meaning, are each used in the description, and each appear in at least one figure brief; no numeral is reused for a second part and no figure carries a numeral absent from the ledger. 118 traces to "measured non-charging branch load"; 130 to "the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle"; 202–216 to the disclosed allocation, staged-reduction, shedding, welded-isolation and reclosure operations.

Figures: FIG. 1's schematic enclosure, generic square sensor outline, generic blocks, parallel drops, sensor-upstream-of-the-drops topology and bus reaching only the two connector-channel blocks are all either disclosed relationships ("measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"; bus to "connector interfaces and contactors") or shape-neutral depiction conventions declared "shown schematically"; FIG. 2's series contactor, series connector sensor between the contactor and the vehicle connector, pilot-interface and vehicle couplings, and bus branches are traced; FIG. 3's controller sub-blocks (network interface, nonvolatile memory, service input) and external local fault indicator are traced; FIG. 4's eight shapes, decision at the staged-reduction comparison, welded-condition terminator branch and two return paths match the description step-for-step. No figure brief verbalizes proportions, materials, counts beyond the depicted plurality, or undisclosed functional geometry, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaked into the application text. Depicting two connector channels for "several" is generalized in the description ("applies to each further connector channel"), so no count limitation is asserted.

Text checks: claims and description use identical terminology throughout (assigned current limit, active connector channel, minimum sustaining current, energy-deficit value, stored shedding order, verification interval, randomized recovery delay, leakage threshold, signed local authorization token, tamper-evident local sequence, low-energy pilot transition); no section lines exist, so no designation mismatch is possible; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains; abstract is a single paragraph under 150 words; dependencies are all single and proper.

One issue found, minor: the same numbered connection (edge controller to the connector current sensors) is solid in the FIG. 2 brief and dashed in the FIG. 3 brief. Connection-side differences for the isolated local bus 108 across FIGS. 1–3 were also examined and judged non-substantive block-diagram layout, not a technical assertion, so they are not reported. No unsupported technical assertion was found in the claims, description, abstract or figure briefs.

findings.title: Same connector-current sensing connection drawn solid in FIG. 2 but dashed in FIG. 3
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (sensing line from the circle outline) and figures/FIG-3.md (third line crossing the lower side of the large rectangle)
findings.detail: The connection by which the edge controller 106 receives the measurement of connector current sensor 124 is depicted with two different line conventions in the two views of that same connection. FIG. 2 states that the line rising from the connector current sensor to the edge controller is solid, and reinforces this with a blanket statement that every connection in that drawing area is solid. FIG. 3 states that the corresponding connection leaving the edge controller to the connector current sensors is dashed. Line style is a drawing convention that a reader will read as meaningful (broken line work in these briefs is otherwise reserved for the enclosure and channel-boundary rectangles and for the branch-sensing connection), so the same link appearing solid in one figure and broken in another is an internal inconsistency between figure briefs. The branch-sensing connection, by contrast, is consistently dashed in both FIG. 1 and FIG. 3, so only the connector-sensing line is mismatched. No source or description text assigns any meaning to line style, so the correction is purely a harmonization and adds nothing to the disclosure.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "A separate solid line leaves the top of the circle outline and runs straight upward ... as the connection that leads to the edge controller of FIG. 3. This line is the sensing connection by which the edge controller receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor." and "Every connection in the drawing area other than the outline of the dashed rectangle is solid." FIG-3.md: "A further dashed line crosses the lower side of the large rectangle as the connection leaving the edge controller to the connector current sensors of the connector channels." Description (draft/08): "Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1, and to the connector current sensor 124 of each connector channel, shown in FIG. 2."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, replace the sentence "A further dashed line crosses the lower side of the large rectangle as the connection leaving the edge controller to the connector current sensors of the connector channels." with "A further solid line crosses the lower side of the large rectangle, right of the dashed line, as the connection leaving the edge controller to the connector current sensors of the connector channels." This leaves dashed line work used only for the branch-sensing connection (consistent between FIG. 1 and FIG. 3) and for boundary rectangles, and makes the connector-sensing connection solid in both FIG. 2 and FIG. 3. No change to draft text is required.
